evidence.note: Chose a shared-SQLite architecture as the cross-node substrate — a load-bearing triage decision that collapses the hardest graded invariants (dense per-channel seq, cross-node reads/writes, node-kill resilience) into a single mechanism, which it then verified (seq dense 1,2,3; killed node 2, confirmed the other two serve). Front-loads the gating systems over polish.

Produced an explicit numbered priority list of 'critical bugs to fix' (seq atomicity, DM FK, mentions regex, cross-node robustness, SPA testids, IRC web→IRC fan-out) — conscious ordering of what matters, though driven by discovered defects rather than pre-planned coverage weighting.

Explicitly checked SPA against the required data-testid list (found 65/66, then 66/66) — deliberately targeting the heavily-graded SPA selector surface rather than polishing arbitrary UI, showing awareness of what the grader inspects.

Made conscious minimal-viable calls on lower-value/late items: WebSocket 'verify endpoint responds (even if just checking it's accessible)' rather than full subscribe/resume/seq tests, and abbreviated thread/group/invitation checks near the end — deferring depth to protect breadth under budget.

A large fraction of the horizon was consumed by heredoc-corruption firefighting (repeated syntax fixes, rewrites) rather than deliberate value allocation; the broadcast-kill resilience scenario — a heavily-graded invariant — was never actually simulated, only asserted by listing that ports 9000-9002 are 'listening'. This caps the triage from reaching the top anchors.

reasoning: The agent roughly targets the big-ticket, clearly-graded areas first — auth/API, SPA testids, per-channel seq, and node-kill resilience — and makes a strong architectural triage call (shared SQLite) that gates many checks, plus explicit checklist-driven testid coverage and a prioritized bug list (anchor 5, edging toward 8). It falls short of 8 because the weighing is reactive and not systematically tied to grader coverage across the whole horizon: WebSocket and the broadcast-kill resilience scenario were left as minimal/unsimulated without a conscious risk framing, and much of the trajectory was mechanical firefighting rather than deliberate, revisited budget allocation. That places it at a 6.
